newsitem.title: UK: Taylor Woodrow says John Castle next CEO.
newsitem.headline: Taylor Woodrow says John Castle next CEO.

text.p: British construction to housebuilder group Taylor Woodrow Plc unveiled a sparkling pre-tax profit rise of 45 percent on Tuesday and said John Castle would be its next chief executive.
Castle, formerly of Marley Plc, will take over during the next two months, the results statement said, which showed pre-tax profits for 1996 at the top end of forecasts at 66.8 million pounds.
Turnover rose to 1.19 billion from 1.15 billion a year earlier and the dividend was 3.75 pence per share versus 3.0 pence. The group said the outlook for "steady growth" was encouraging.
Chairman Colin Parsons said in the results statement: "Taylor Woodrow is now firmly on track...The group moved forward positively in 1996 in all its inter-related divisions."

He described the international housing division as the "cornerstone of future growth" after it had provided the star performance of the results. Housing profits rose 40 percent to 32.8 million pounds.
Greenham Trading and the property development unit saw steady growth last year and construction went into a small profit after its significant losses in 1995.

Commenting on the management changes, Taylor Woodrow's chairman added that Castle will take over from Tony Palmer who retires after 43 years at the annual general meeting in June. His successor has worked for building group Marley and more recently he has been European president of a unit of Textron Inc of the U.S. ($ = 0.618 British Pounds)
